label: Highly distressed, heavy-use graduate-educated women
summary: This profile is characterized by comparatively higher loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Respondents in this group also tend to be female, have graduate-level education or higher, and report more than 5 hours of use.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate degree or above, more than 5 hours of use
behavior_markers: Tends to be a heavy-use respondent
More likely anchored in a highly educated female subgroup

label: Low loneliness, low depression, low anxiety
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively low loneliness, low depressive symptoms, and very low anxiety symptoms across the measured indicators.
demographic_anchor: Typically male, educated to graduate level or above, with 1-3 hours as the referenced time-use category.
behavior_markers: Reports relatively low loneliness on the UCLA-8 measure
Shows low depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9
Shows very low anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7
Represents a comparatively low-distress respondent group

label: Profile 2: Lonely but emotionally lower-symptom
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively higher loneliness while showing comparatively lower average depressive and anxiety symptoms. The pattern suggests social disconnection is more prominent than broad internalizing distress.
demographic_anchor: More commonly represented by women with graduate-level education or higher who report 1-3 hours.
behavior_markers: Reports relatively elevated loneliness on the UCLA-8 measure.
Shows comparatively low average depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9.
Shows comparatively low average anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7.
Presents a profile where loneliness stands out more than depression or anxiety.
tone: Socially disconnected yet generally emotionally stable relative to more symptomatic groups.
